memory_lessons.applicability: A matched spatial-only control is needed to distinguish temporal reuse from the effects of tiling and parallel scheduling.
memory_lessons.claim: The halo-aware candidate was correct and measured 0.2963455 seconds; the supplied baseline was correct and measured 0.464905 seconds. Without a matched spatial-only tiled candidate, these measurements do not establish that temporal reuse caused the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this spatial-only control and compare it with the halo-aware candidate at one and four threads.

proposal.hypothesis: The prior halo-aware six-step candidate was correct and measured 0.2963455 seconds versus the correct baseline's 0.464905 seconds, but that comparison does not isolate temporal reuse. This 64^3 spatial-only control uses the same radius-three stencil arithmetic and static collapsed OpenMP tile schedule across six globally synchronized steps. Comparing its one- and four-thread timings with the halo-aware candidate will test whether temporal reuse adds benefit beyond spatial tiling; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Retain the radius-three spatial stencil arithmetic and partition the baseline update region into clipped 64^3 tiles for each timestep.
Run the six timesteps in one OpenMP parallel region with a static collapsed three-dimensional tile loop and its implicit per-step barrier.
Preserve full even/odd output initialization and the baseline's unchanged boundaries; this spatial-only control allocates no temporal scratch.
